The data point to B. Toracal dysfunction behaves like a downstream summary of the thoracic radiculopathies, so L T6 radiculopathy is more likely the cause.

I checked this by comparing "toracal dysfunction" with the columns for thoracic radiculopathy (L and R, T1 to T12). In 94% of the 16,384 patients, dysfunction equals "any thoracic radiculopathy is present". That deterministic-looking dependence suggests the radiculopathies feed into the dysfunction label.

L T6 radiculopathy itself is very rare: only 1 patient in 16,384 has it, so the pairwise table for the two labels is too sparse to say much on its own.

ANSWER: B
